status_summary: NIST released a statement dated 2025-12-11 (updated 2026-01-16) saying the Department of Commerce had finalized agreements to transfer management and operations of the Baldrige Award process, the Quest for Excellence conference, framework revisions and the Executive Fellows Program to the Alliance for Performance Excellence and the Baldrige Foundation, starting with the 2026 award cycle. The 2026 cycle has run under that arrangement: the Alliance, administering the award on behalf of NIST, opened intent-to-apply on 2026-03-19 and named 13 finalists on 2026-07-10, and minutes of the Baldrige Board of Overseers meeting of 2026-06-11 describe the memorandum, a reduced applicant fee and an expected loss of federal appropriations. NIST and Commerce keep ultimate responsibility under 15 U.S.C. 3711a, and the handover is split between two partners rather than made wholly to the Foundation.

timeline.event: NIST announced finalized agreements transferring management and operations of the award process, the Quest for Excellence conference, framework revisions and the Executive Fellows Program to two private-sector partners, beginning with the 2026 award cycle; NIST retains ultimate responsibility for the framework and award process.

title: Hand the Baldrige Performance Excellence Program to the Baldrige Foundation
uncertainties: The NIST page states its release date and an update date in the page text; a news article is dated 2025-12-16. Operation of the 2026 cycle by the partners rests on Alliance announcements published on the Baldrige Foundation site and on NIST's June 2026 overseers minutes; the Alliance's own site was not read. These partner announcements are acts of private administrators under the agreement, so they are cited as sources rather than entered as government actions in the timeline. The minutes call the instrument both a memorandum of agreement and a memorandum of understanding, mention a reduced applicant fee without amounts, and record that federal appropriations are expected to be lost and that the model carries risks; they do not list the duties NIST keeps. The minutes were signed on 2026-07-10 and the meeting date matches the April 2026 Federal Register notice. The handover is split, with the award process going to the Alliance and the conference, framework and fellows to the Foundation, so it is not wholly to the Foundation as the Mandate text asks. Appropriations language for FY2026 or FY2027 was not checked. Inference: progress of 70 reflects confirmed operation by non-government staff on fees, short of full transfer.
